ambiguity_notes: 'Active' does NOT mean energetic, busy, or vigorous. It means 'through the active states of the blanket' -- the half of the blanket the interior writes to. A register that renders it with a vigour/energy root has named the wrong thing.

The English name misleads even in English: it reads as though 'inference' were the noun and 'active' a flavour of it. The concept is the reverse claim -- that action IS inference, not that there is a lively kind of inference.

Sanskrit anumāna carries heavy Nyāya freight: it is one of the pramāṇas (means of valid knowledge) and in that system it is a syllogistic, five-membered public procedure with a fixed structure (pratijñā, hetu, udāharaṇa, upanaya, nigamana). Active inference is a continuous variational optimisation, not a syllogism. The freight is real and is not neutralised by the compound.

IN THE UNI PROGRAM this is the framing LENS and not a running mechanism: no AIF loop exists in the Rust crate and G is not computed as a scheduler. A rendering in any register that implies UNI runs active inference is drift, regardless of how good the philology is.

forbidden_mistranslations.why_wrong: Reverses the claim. Action is not the OBJECT of the inference; action is one of the two routes by which the same quantity is minimized. A genitive/objective reading destroys the concept.

MW gives buddhi as 'intelligence, reason, intellect, mind, discernment, judgement' and it is the Sāṃkhya Intellect -- a tattva, an evolute of prakṛti. It imports a whole metaphysics and an experiencer. The formalism admits partitions for a Newton's cradle.
Ratiocinatio names discursive human reasoning. The scheme is not a style of reasoning and applies to systems that do not reason at all.
A different, established machine-learning term (querying an oracle for labels). Collision would silently reroute the reader to a different literature.

F is a functional (it eats a function q and returns a scalar), not a function of a number. Registers with a strong noun/verb distinction should not render it as an act of measuring; it is the measure yielded.

ambiguity_notes: THE DEFINING TRAP: surprisal is NOT the felt emotion of surprise. A register that renders it with an affect root asserts an experiencer, and CONCEPTS.json names that as a lane-crossing -- the cardinal sin of merging the TRUE and HONEST stores. -ln p(o) is defined for a thermostat and for a burning fuse, neither of which is surprised by anything.

The English word 'surprisal' is a deliberate technical coinage precisely to hold this fence: information theorists did not say 'surprise'. Any register that reaches for its ordinary surprise-word has undone the work the English coinage did, and this is why the Sanskrit above takes a mātrā (quantity) head rather than a vismaya (wonder) head.

Distinct from ENTROPY, which is EXPECTED surprisal -- the average of this quantity over the distribution. Surprisal attaches to ONE observation; entropy attaches to a distribution. No register may merge them.

Surprisal is relative to a MODEL, never absolute. -ln p(o) presupposes the p. The same observation carries different surprisal under different models, so a register implying an intrinsic property of the event is wrong.

A register reaching for a fertility/begetting root -- which the Sanskrit janaka literally is, MW giving 'begetting' and m. 'a progenitor, father' -- must fence that sense off explicitly.

'Model' in the ordinary senses -- an exemplar to be imitated, a person who poses, a scale replica -- are all live homonyms in every one of these five registers. The Latin 'exemplar' is especially exposed: its ordinary sense is a pattern to be COPIED, which reverses the direction of fit.

ambiguity_notes: THIS ENTRY IS A RECEIPT, and that is its whole job: it is the receipt for the INADMISSIBLE claim 'a low F means the model is correct'. It explains why a CONFIDENTLY WRONG model can sit at low F. A register that renders it as a mere technical slack term, without the epistemic sting, has translated the algebra and lost the point.

THE SELF-SWALLOWING PROPERTY, which is the hardest thing to carry into any register: the gap is UNOBSERVABLE without the very posterior that was intractable to begin with. You cannot measure how wrong you are, because measuring it requires the thing you could not compute. A register implying it could be evaluated, monitored, or bounded in practice asserts the opposite of the concept.

'Gap' is not a hole, a breach, a lack, a deficiency, or a failure. It is non-negative slack in an inequality. In particular it is not a defect to be fixed: it is zero only in the limiting case q = p(s|o).

'Bound' here is a mathematical upper bound, NOT a tie, a fetter, a limit-in-the-sense-of-restriction, or an obligation. Sanskrit bandha and Hindi 'bandh' both carry the fetter sense strongly (bandha is bondage in Yoga/Vedānta soteriology -- heavy doctrinal freight), and the Hindi rendering above is exposed to it.

The gap IS a KL divergence, D_KL[q||p(s|o)], so this entry inherits every ambiguity note from KL_DIVERGENCE -- in particular its asymmetry. A register that renders it as a symmetric distance asserts a false mathematical property here too.

ambiguity_notes: THE TRAP, AND IT IS SUBTLE AND SEVERE: this is the TECHNICAL sense, not the ordinary 'correctness' sense. CONCEPTS.json makes the sting explicit -- a CONFABULATED OBSERVATION RAISES APPARENT ACCURACY while corrupting the model, which is exactly what the complexity term prices. So 'accuracy' here measures fit to the observations you actually got, INCLUDING fabricated ones. It is not a virtue and it is not correctness.

THIS IS WHY THE ATTESTED LATIN WORD WAS DECLINED. Lewis & Short s.v. 'accuratio' (retrieved 2026-07-15) gives 'accuracy, exactness, carefulness (very rare)' -- from accuro, 'to do with care'. That is the ordinary sense of careful workmanship: a virtue of the person doing the work. F's accuracy term is a property of a fit, and a careless liar can have a high one. A CITED headword that carries the WRONG SENSE is not a licence; it is a trap with a citation attached, and it is the most dangerous kind.

Not 'accuracy' in the measurement-science sense either, where accuracy (closeness to the true value) is contrasted with precision (repeatability). That contrast is a THIRD distinct sense, and it collides with the separate concept PRECISION in this same domain. Three senses of this word pair are live at once.

The decomposition is COMPLEXITY MINUS ACCURACY, and F is MINIMIZED -- so accuracy enters NEGATIVELY and minimizing F pushes accuracy UP. A register that renders accuracy as a cost or penalty inverts the sign. It is the term you want large.

Accuracy is an expectation under q, E_q(s)[ln p(o|s)] -- it is averaged over the belief, not evaluated at a point estimate. A register implying a single best-guess state is being scored has dropped the expectation.

Citing a real dictionary entry does not make a rendering admissible -- the sense must match too, and here it does not.

MW s.v. yathārtha (retrieved 2026-07-15): 'accordant with reality, conformable to truth'. It asserts correspondence to REALITY. F's accuracy is correspondence to the OBSERVATIONS RECEIVED, which may be false. Using it would make the corpus's own warning -- that a confabulated observation raises apparent accuracy -- self-contradictory in Sanskrit.
Purity/correctness roots, and samyak- carries heavy Buddhist freight (the samyak- terms of the Eightfold Path). Both assert rightness.
Collides head-on with the separately registered concept PRECISION in this same domain, which is inverse variance. Two different quantities would share one word in a single lexicon.

ambiguity_notes: THE DEFINING TRAP, named in CONCEPTS.json: this is SHANNON entropy, NOT thermodynamic entropy. The shared English word is a loan, and a register that reaches for a heat/disorder root imports a false physical claim. This is the same class of error as rendering 'free energy' thermodynamically, and the two traps compound: a reader who takes both loans literally will conclude the free-energy principle is a statement of thermodynamics. It is not.

'Entropy as disorder' is a further, popular-science mistranslation that is wrong even WITHIN thermodynamics and is catastrophic here. H is the average uncertainty of outcomes under a distribution. A uniform distribution over two tidy outcomes has higher entropy than a peaked distribution over a thousand messy ones. Disorder is not the variable.

Entropy is EXPECTED SURPRISAL: it is the average of SURPRISAL over the distribution. Surprisal attaches to ONE observation; entropy attaches to a DISTRIBUTION. CONCEPTS.json marks these distinct and no register may merge them. The Sanskrit coinage above is deliberately built out of the surprisal coinage to make the relation visible while keeping the terms separate.

Entropy is not information, and not 'amount of information' in the loose sense. It is also not negentropy, not information CONTENT of a message, and not compressibility -- though all are relatives. It is a property of a distribution, not of a string or an object.

In this domain entropy appears chiefly INSIDE other quantities -- most importantly as AMBIGUITY, which is the expected entropy of the likelihood, E_q(s|pi)[H[p(o|s)]]. A register's entropy word must survive being nested inside that expression.

Risk is a divergence, so it inherits KL_DIVERGENCE's asymmetry fence: D_KL[q(o|pi)||p(o|C)] is not symmetric, and it is not a distance between predicted and preferred outcomes in any metric sense.

ambiguity_notes: A LIVE TRAP FOR THIS VERY FILE, and CONCEPTS.json says so explicitly: this is NOT linguistic or semantic ambiguity -- and THIS LEXICON'S OWN ambiguity_notes FIELDS USE THE ORDINARY SENSE. So the word 'ambiguity' appears in this file with two incompatible meanings: the field name means 'senses a word wrongly carries', and this concept means E_q(s|pi)[H[p(o|s)]]. That collision is inside the schema itself and cannot be renamed away here; it is recorded so no reader mistakes one for the other.

THE DEFINING PROPERTY: high ambiguity means YOU ACT AND STILL DO NOT KNOW WHERE YOU ARE. It is not that the words are unclear -- it is that the WORLD's mapping from states to observations is uninformative. You can reach exactly the state you intended and learn nothing by arriving.

It is a property of the LIKELIHOOD p(o|s) -- of the A tensor, of the sensor -- and NOT a mental state. Doubt, hesitation, indecision, and confusion are all states of a mind; ambiguity is a fact about a channel. A blurry camera has high ambiguity and no doubts. Every doubt-root in every register fails on exactly this point, which is why they are all forbidden below.

Ambiguity is one of the TWO terms of G, with RISK the other: G = risk + ambiguity. It is also (up to sign) the epistemic term. Minimizing G therefore includes REDUCING ambiguity, which is what makes an agent probe, disambiguate, and look before it leaps. A register that renders it as mere vagueness will not carry that.

'Expected' here is again the mathematical expectation operator, taken under q(s|pi) -- so all the traps at EXPECTED_FREE_ENERGY apply inside this term too. And 'entropy' here is Shannon entropy, so ENTROPY's heat/disorder fence applies as well. This one short concept inherits two other entries' fences.

ambiguity_notes: SAME QUANTITY AS F WITH THE SIGN FLIPPED, and CONCEPTS.json is emphatic: A REGISTER MUST NOT PRESENT THEM AS TWO MECHANISMS. The machine-learning literature MAXIMIZES the ELBO where the active-inference literature MINIMIZES F. Two communities, two sign conventions, ONE quantity. A reader who meets both and concludes there are two things has been misled by vocabulary alone.

THE ENTRY INHERITS EVIDENCE'S SOVEREIGN HOMONYM AND MAKES IT WORSE: 'evidence' here is p(o), the marginal likelihood -- NOT evidence in the method sense (receipts, EVIDENCE_CLASS). 'Evidence lower bound' therefore reads, to anyone in this corpus, as though it bounded how well-evidenced a claim is. It does not. It bounds a model's normalizing constant. The Hindi calque above uses 'sākṣya' (testimony) and is flagged as probably failing on exactly this.

'Lower bound' means it sits BELOW ln p(o) and rises toward it. Contrast BOUND_GAP, where F sits ABOVE surprisal. Same slack, opposite direction, because of the sign flip -- and a register that renders 'bound' identically in both places without the direction will confuse them.
'Bound' is a mathematical bound, not a fetter, tie, or obligation. Same fence as BOUND_GAP; Hindi 'paribandh' and Sanskrit bandha both carry the fetter sense.

ELBO is an acronym in English and is frequently left untranslated in every language, including in Hindi and Spanish technical writing. That is a defensible treatment -- like 'nat', it is a name -- but unlike 'nat' it is an acronym whose expansion carries the trap, so leaving it opaque HIDES the evidence homonym rather than resolving it.

ambiguity_notes: ITS STATUS IS GENUINELY CONTESTED AND BOTH DIRECTIONS MUST TRAVEL. CONCEPTS.json is unusually careful here and this entry must not simplify it: (1) demanding the FEP itself be falsifiable is a CATEGORY ERROR (Andrews 2021), because it designates a model structure; AND (2) a model structure IS NOT AN EMPIRICAL FINDING. Specific process-theory models built on it are falsifiable; the structure is not. NEITHER MAY BORROW THE OTHER'S CREDIT. A register that lets the FEP read as an established empirical law has taken a side; so has one that lets it read as unfalsifiable pseudoscience. Both are wrong.

'PRINCIPLE' IS THE PROBLEM WORD IN EVERY REGISTER. In English it can mean a law of nature (the uncertainty principle), a rule of conduct (a person of principle), a foundational assumption (first principles), or an organising idea. The FEP is closest to the third. Sanskrit siddhānta -- the author's own proposal -- means an ESTABLISHED CONCLUSION of a school, which leans toward the first and second and probably OVERCLAIMS. It is flagged for that reason.

IT IS A PROPOSAL, and the definition says so. Not a discovery, not a law, not a finding, not a theorem. A register whose word for 'principle' implies discovery has upgraded a model structure into an empirical result, which is precisely the move both CONCEPTS.json and the honesty rail forbid.

'Free energy' carries the same physics-loan fence as everywhere else in this file: a heat/energy root imports a false physical claim. The Hindi and Spanish calques take the energy root and the conflict is recorded, as at VARIATIONAL_FREE_ENERGY.

'Non-equilibrium steady state' is a technical condition from statistical physics and is not decoration: the claim is scoped to systems at NESS. A register that drops the qualifier renders a much stronger and much less defensible claim -- that everything minimizes free energy.

RENDERED AS A SENTENCE, NOT A COMPOUND, ON PURPOSE: a compound like karma-anumāna would read as 'inference about action' or 'action-type inference' -- an objective-genitive or descriptive reading that REVERSES the claim. The emphatic eva forces the identity reading, which is the concept's entire content: action is not a topic of inference and not a kind of inference; it IS inference, run through the other half of the blanket.

ambiguity_notes: 'AS' IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM AND IT IS INVISIBLE IN ENGLISH. The English 'action as inference' can be read three ways: (1) action resembling inference (simile -- wrong); (2) action considered in its capacity as inference (identity -- CORRECT); (3) action in the role of inference (functional substitute -- wrong, it is not a stand-in). Spanish 'como' has the same three-way ambiguity, which is why the Sanskrit and Hindi above force the identity reading with an emphatic particle instead.

ACTION IS NOT A FACULTY BOLTED ONTO INFERENCE; it is inference run through the other half of the blanket. CONCEPTS.json puts it exactly that way. A register that renders this as a comparison, an analogy, or a metaphor has turned a structural consequence into a figure of speech.

THE PREFERENCE C IS WHAT BREAKS THE TIE between the two routes, and the entry is incomplete without it. Both routes minimize the same quantity, so the formalism ALONE does not say whether to shiver or to believe you are warm. Read with PREFERENCE; the thermoregulation case is what makes the tie-break non-optional.

'Changing active states until the world fits the model' is not wishful thinking and not self-deception -- it is ACTING. The phrasing invites a misreading in which the agent simply decides the world is different. The active states are the real output channel; the world really changes.

'Prediction error' is a term this corpus CUT from the concept list as redundant (it appears in the cut_as_redundant list of CONCEPTS.json), yet the definition of THIS concept uses the phrase. That is a small internal tension in the source and is recorded here rather than silently smoothed: this entry's definition depends on a term the backbone deliberately does not register.

forbidden_mistranslations.why_wrong: It is an identity, not a comparison. The blanket partition makes action a route of inference, not a thing resembling one.

Reads as 'inference about action' (objective genitive) or 'action-type inference' (descriptive) -- both reverse or dilute the claim. This is why the entry is a sentence with eva rather than a compound.
